teaser: pki.sgit.ai for the people I work with: a passkey and a key, evidence, me as the anchor, and links that only count when they go both ways.
core_idea: sgit has keys but no directory or web of trust, so pki.sgit.ai should register people: a passkey opens a vault holding their key pair, they publish the public half with evidence, Dinis verifies first, and links between people count only when both confirm in their own records, which stops the 2019 flooding attack; the point is to find someone and send them a secret by QR code.

figures.caption: From a passkey to a message. A person registers a passkey on pki.sgit.ai, which opens their vault; makes or imports a key pair, with the private keys kept in the vault; publishes the public half; adds evidence (a website, GitHub, a DNS record); is verified by Dinis, who signs it, and confirms that from their side; and links with others, each link counting only when both confirm. Then anyone in the register can be sent a secret as a QR code that opens in their browser and is read with their vault.

Two ways, or not at all. On the left, 2019: anyone could append a signature to anyone's key, and nothing could be deleted, so keys were flooded until they broke. On the right, the rule here: each person writes only to their own record. A vouches for B in A's record; B confirms in B's record; the link exists only when both do. A vouch that nobody confirms stays a claim in the voucher's own record, and each record has a size limit.
